  "text": "Tobias waited until the church clock struck eight before he took the road to Maren's house. He carried the loaf she had asked him to bring. Under his arm the paper had gone soft with warmth.

The door was shut.

He knocked, then waited, then set the loaf on the porch rail. From there he could see all eleven posts descending to the beach. Nothing hung between them. He remembered a lantern, but remembering was not the same as having something to tell.

At the front window he cupped his hands against the glass.

The lamp stood on the sill, unlit. Beyond it were the chair, the cold grate, the place where her father's rug had lain. The bare boards were lighter there.

He went back to the door and tried the latch. It held.

For a while he stood with his thumb on it. Then he took the loaf from the rail and put it on the step, where she would have to see it coming out.

At the bend he met the boy who delivered coal.

'Is she in?'

'I couldn't say.'

The boy went on. Tobias stayed until he heard the cart stop, then made himself walk.

That afternoon the loaf was still there. By evening someone had covered it with an upturned basin against the rain.

No one admitted to doing this.

For several mornings Tobias lifted the basin and put his hand against the paper. On the fourth he brought another loaf. He took the old one home without looking at its underside.",
